question: Within each tool family, does outline shape in the dated record change gradually (random walk or trend), stay put (stasis), settle toward an optimum (OU), or jump between stable periods (punctuation)?
note: Registered after an exploratory four-model fit (stasis, URW, GRW, punctuation) inside the latent-decoder evaluation had been seen. At registration the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model and the model-recovery simulation were added; data, trait, bins, thresholds and the other four models are unchanged from that fit. Descriptive: catalog dates are attributions with ranges, the record is what museums kept (almost entirely one museum at present), and a family mixes sub-types whose share changes over time, so a fitted jump can come from collecting or cataloguing history rather than design history.

model_descriptions.stasis: Hunt 2007: independent fluctuation around one mean (theta, omega)
model_descriptions.GRW: Hunt 2006: directional random walk (anc, mu_step, sigma2_step)
model_descriptions.OU: Hunt, Bell and Travis 2008: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck approach to an optimum (anc, theta, alpha, sigma2)
model_descriptions.punctuation: Hunt 2008: two stasis segments with one shift, shared omega; shift searched over positions leaving at least 3 bins per segment (theta1, theta2, omega, shift)

selection: AICc (Hurvich and Tsai 1989) and Akaike weights
recovery_design: for every fitted 25-year series and every model, simulate 100 series from that model with its fitted parameters at the same bin times and sampling errors (seed 17), refit all five models, and record which one wins

references.text: Eldredge N, Gould SJ (1972) Punctuated equilibria: an alternative to phyletic gradualism. In Schopf TJM (ed) Models in Paleobiology, pp 82-115. Freeman, Cooper, San Francisco.
Hunt G (2006) Fitting and comparing models of phyletic evolution: random walks and beyond. Paleobiology 32(4).
Hunt G (2007) The relative importance of directional change, random walks, and stasis in the evolution of fossil lineages. PNAS 104(47):18404-18408.
Hunt G (2008) Gradual or pulsed evolution: when should punctuational explanations be preferred? Paleobiology 34(3):360-377.
Hunt G, Bell MA, Travis MP (2008) Evolution toward a new adaptive optimum: phenotypic evolution in a fossil stickleback lineage. Evolution 62(3):700-710.
Hunt G, Hopkins MJ, Lidgard S (2015) Simple versus complex models of trait evolution and stasis as a response to environmental change. PNAS 112(16):4885-4890.
Hurvich CM, Tsai CL (1989) Regression and time series model selection in small samples. Biometrika 76(2):297-307.
Valverde S, Solé RV (2015) Punctuated equilibrium in the large-scale evolution of programming languages. J R Soc Interface 12(107):20150249.

context: In fossil lineages, directional change was best supported in about 5% of more than 250 trait sequences, with the rest split roughly evenly between random walk and stasis (Hunt 2007); with more models and longer series, stasis remained common, directional change was 13%, and complex (punctuated or mode-shifting) models were often favoured for long sequences (Hunt, Hopkins & Lidgard 2015).
